summary: A card for a paper bracer you cut yourself. Twelve panels off one A2 sheet lock together with tabs, and the pleated top opens into a fan. The page its address opens is where corrections land.
license_note: CC-BY-NC-4.0 is what this card's own #vc-card block declares — read in the tree at src/site/aurea/index.html and again from the live page on 2026-08-17, both giving license CC-BY-NC-4.0 and replication noncommercial. It covers the design: the panel geometry, the cut sheet, and the two card faces. It is NOT the parent repository's grant. LICENSE at the root of mrdirno/vibe-cards is MIT (GitHub's repository API returns spdx_id MIT, fetched anonymously 2026-08-17) and covers the code. NOTICE at that same root removes this card's ten artwork files from the MIT grant BY NAME — src/site/aurea/card-front.png, card-back.png, src/web/cards/aurea-front.png, aurea-back.png, the four examples/aurea-card/designs/*.png, and examples/aurea-card/assets/front_editorial.png and back_blueprint.png; all ten checked present in the tree 2026-08-17 — in one entry with card 001's and card 004's, thirty files. NOTICE is served at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/NOTICE.txt (200 on 2026-08-17, against a 404 control on the same host). Nothing in this manifest enlarges what NOTICE withholds, and nothing here grants anything. The NonCommercial terms themselves are the full CC BY-NC 4.0 legal code at examples/aurea-card/LICENSE: fetched creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/legalcode.txt on 2026-08-17 and compared byte for byte — identical, sha256 41003d4a74749c0220e33dd415042164b5a1093ed401f36277234f772d22d3d0, 19,347 bytes. In plain terms, and as the card's replication field declares: print this card, cut this bracer, remix the sheet, teach a class with it — credit it, and do not sell it or anything made from it. One gap a reader should know about: that licence file is in the repository and is NOT served under this card's url. /aurea/LICENSE, /aurea/LICENSE.txt and /examples/aurea-card/LICENSE all returned 404 on 2026-08-17; the page carries the terms only as a link out to creativecommons.org.
origin: Not a fork and not a repository of its own: /aurea/ is a page-project inside mrdirno/vibe-cards, the seed repo of this registry, published on that repo's Pages surface — GitHub's API returns fork=false, private=false, created 2026-08-10, fetched anonymously 2026-08-17. THE CARD ITSELF DID NOT ORIGINATE HERE. Its raw material arrived as a package from an external, autonomous card-generation run, identified in this tree only by RUN_ID "PB-48-14-09" (examples/aurea-card/tools/build_card.py:58). The sibling package for card 001 names the shape plainly at the head of examples/manis-card/tools/build_card.py: "THE ARRIVING PACKAGE put its kicker underneath a circular photo inset... The assets and the palette are good and are kept. The layout is not." The commit that brought card 002 in — 8d56058, 2026-08-15T14:17:15-07:00, "Two more cards for the book, and the dropdown now has a folder for it instead of filing them next to strangers" — says "EVERY NUMBER PRINTED ON A CARD IS READ OFF ITS OWN DRAWING, not off the prose that shipped beside it" and "Where a package's spec and its drawing disagreed on material, the card names both rather than picking the one that reads better." That one commit added examples/aurea-card/assets/front_editorial.png (2,729,173 bytes) and back_blueprint.png (2,046,745 bytes) together, with no README and no docs/ — the package still has neither, only assets/, designs/, package/, tools/ and LICENSE. The arriving run's own series log survives beside a later card, examples/aurelia-card/docs/ITINERARY.md: same PB-* run-id namespace, and its cards point at a "kikko.craftworks" host that is not this project's. WHAT THIS REPO AUTHORED is the composition and the page: examples/aurea-card/tools/build_card.py re-lays both faces (crop windows, safe zone, and the back's three-column band), and src/site/aurea/index.html is written here. The front image is a generated render — a forearm and a hand wearing the bracer, no face and no identifiable person, declared on the page and in the #vc-card provenance field per docs/CARDS.md §8; I opened src/site/aurea/card-front.png and what is printed matches the declaration, brass cuff hinges and amber bead pins included, which the page also discloses as disagreeing with the sheet. ONE SOURCE IS MISSING FROM THE TREE: build_card.py:30 cites VIBE_CARD_SPEC.json for the 78 g weight and the washi-laminate material name, and `find . -name 'VIBE_CARD_SPEC*'` on 2026-08-17 returns only examples/aurelia-card/docs/VIBE_CARD_SPEC.json, which belongs to card 004. Those two figures therefore rest on a document that was never committed here.
_note: WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT THIS PATH. Measured 2026-08-17, before it did: https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/aurea/wish-it-better.json returned 404 while https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/wish-it-better.json returned 200 on the same host in the same run, against a 404 control under /aurea/. Criterion 4 reads the listed url for a page-project, and this card is not in network.json's listed[] (5 entries on 2026-08-17, none of them this one). It is hand-authored and committed BEFORE listing on purpose: tools/build_site.py can derive a manifest, but only for entries already in listed[], so a derived one would be produced by the act of listing and criterion 4 would be satisfying itself. src/site/gt/wish-it-better.json is the precedent — the only prior page-project manifest, hand-written and committed before GT-001 was listed. LEVEL L0, three clauses, each measured. (1) "This file present" — WISH_IT_BETTER.md is at the repo root and served at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/WISH_IT_BETTER.md, 200 on 2026-08-17 with a 404 control on the same host; tools/build_site.py fails the build without it. (2) "A wish channel that works" — this page's own well, not the landing page's. The live bytes carry data-wish-well once, on the send button, which is the marker §4 requires before an https channel is accepted; the form takes a wish with no account, no email address and no mail client. A read-only GET on the endpoint the page posts to returned 200 with [] while a nonsense table on the same host returned 404, so the table exists and the public key cannot read the queue — what insert-only RLS looks like from outside. I did NOT send a wish: an insert writes to a live queue. (3) "A LICENSE" — root LICENSE is real SPDX MIT per GitHub's API, and this card's own CC BY-NC 4.0 legal code is byte-verified (license_note). NOT L1, on both of its clauses. "Wishes reach a terminal state": the machinery is real and has demonstrably moved wishes to shipped and declined, with written decline reasons — tools/wishing_well_actions.log, 20 append-only transitions between 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-15 — but not for this card. That log records timestamp, status, row id and note, and no card id, so it cannot show whether a wish for AUREA-LATTICE-002 was ever received, and the queue is not readable with the public key. A capability proven on other cards is not this card's record. "Every shipped change carries an eval meeting §2": docs/EVALS.md, the file this manifest points at, contains zero case-insensitive matches for "aurea", "AUREA-LATTICE" or "compound craft" (2026-08-17), so this card has no worked example in it. The intake commit does carry real measurement — faces at exactly 2066x1319, the QR decoded off the shipped back face, a pixel scan of the 93 px margin returning zero dark pixels — and that is a good eval; but "every shipped change" is a claim over the eight commits that have touched src/site/aurea/ (four of which also touched examples/aurea-card/), and I audited their subjects, not their evals, one by one. The spec says of its own v1.0.1 amendment that it "earns nobody L2", and that if in doubt L0 is the honest answer. THREE THINGS THE FIELDS CANNOT CARRY. (a) The page prints a sentence its own log refutes. Step 01 warns "at 97% a 12.0 mm tab is 11.6 mm and every joint is loose"; the first log entry below it says the tab and the slot shrink together, so the fit holds and the bracer comes out 3% small. Both are live right now, one above the other. That is the page's design — the chip's address is burned in, so corrections accumulate in the log rather than by rewriting history — but a reader should not mistake the un-corrected step for a checked one. (b) Nobody has built this object. src/site/aurea/entries.json says so in its own _doc: "nothing here was measured off a built object, because nobody has built one." Every number on the page is read off the drawing or is arithmetic on it, and the drawing arrived from somewhere else (see origin). (c) This file outranks a derived one, and it binds. tools/build_site.py keeps an authored manifest and hard-fails if its level disagrees with the level network.json badges, so if this card is ever listed at anything but L0 this file must move with it or the build stops. Its derived alternative would have declared wish_channel <site>/aurea/#wish — an anchor this page does not have: id="wish" appears 0 times in the live bytes and exists only on the landing page. ONE INACCURACY IN A FILE THIS MANIFEST LEANS ON, recorded because leaving it unsaid is how an inventory stops binding. NOTICE's Compound Craft entry describes "The three 645x645 qr_*.png" as NOT withheld. Measured 2026-08-17: examples/aurea-card/assets/qr_placeholder.png is 1118x1118, bloom's is 430x430, and only manis's qr_fallback.png is 645x645. The withholding is unaffected — the same three files are still outside it — but the number is wrong for two of the three. UNVERIFIED, stated so it is not read as checked: no wish has been submitted through this page by me, so the well is proven reachable and account-free but not proven end-to-end for this card; the 78 g weight and the washi-laminate material name have no source in this tree; and no physical build of this bracer exists to check any dimension on the sheet against.
